one_liner: BigCommerce offers broad REST+GraphQL APIs with OAuth app flow and static API-account tokens. Reliable free API access comes through a Partner sandbox, because trial stores reportedly have API access removed. An official MCP server is claimed but not verifiable from the supplied pages.
auth_notes: Apps use an OAuth install/launch flow with a client ID and secret from the Developer Portal. Store-level API accounts (Settings > API Accounts) give a store_hash and access_token, sent in the X-Auth-Token header.
access_notes: The developer homepage says to use a free trial store, but a third-party forum report says trial stores have API access removed (429, quota 0). The dependable free path is the Partner Program: the account is registered immediately and a free Partner sandbox store can be created. Publishing to the App Marketplace needs an approved Technology Partner account. Draft apps can be tested in any store.
blocker_notes: Trial stores may lack API access, so a developer should sign up for the Partner Program to get a sandbox. Each customer store also needs its own API account or app install. Marketplace listing requires partnership approval.
